## Module 5: Working habits

None of these involve new code, but each one decides whether a script still works next month, or on someone else's computer.

**R Markdown.** An `.Rmd` file mixes text with R code and its output -- this course is one. Clicking **Knit** in RStudio runs the code and produces the finished report. You won't need to write one here, but you'll be handed them.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
quiz_question_ui("markdown_quiz", "Someone sends you analysis.Rmd. How do you get the finished report, with the text, code, and results together?", c(
  "Open it in RStudio and click Knit" = "correct",
  "Copy the code chunks into the Console" = "wrong_console",
  "Rename it to analysis.R and click Source" = "wrong_rename"
))
```

**Where scripts live, and paths.** Keep a project's scripts and data together in one folder, opened as an RStudio Project, and use relative paths. Watch for scripts copied from someone else that start with `setwd()` pointing at a folder on *someone else's* computer.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
quiz_question_ui("scripts_quiz", "A script you were sent starts with setwd(\"C:/Users/maria/Desktop/thesis\") and fails on your computer with: cannot change working directory. Why?", c(
  "That folder exists on Maria's computer, not yours" = "correct",
  "You need administrator rights to run setwd()" = "wrong_admin",
  "setwd() needs a package loaded first" = "wrong_package",
  "Windows paths need backslashes, not forward slashes" = "wrong_slashes"
))
```

**File names.** Describe what the file does, in lowercase with `_` or `-` and no spaces: `clean_survey_data.R`, not `final_v2_FINAL.R`.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
quiz_question_ui("naming_files_quiz", "Which of these is the best file name for a script that cleans survey data?", c(
  "clean_survey_data.R" = "correct",
  "Final FINAL script (2).R" = "wrong_final",
  "asdf.R" = "wrong_vague"
))
```

**Version control.** Git (often with GitHub) keeps the full history of every change to a project, so you can see what changed and undo a mistake -- instead of keeping track with file names. You won't use it in this course; just know what it's for.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
quiz_question_ui("version_control_quiz", "What is the main purpose of a version control system like Git?", c(
  "Tracking changes to files over time so you can see history and undo mistakes" = "correct",
  "Automatically fixing bugs in your code" = "wrong_autofix",
  "Making your R scripts run without RStudio installed" = "wrong_standalone"
))
```

## Module 5: Wrapping up

**If you remember only a few things from this module:**

- `ggplot(data, aes(...)) + geom_...()`. Inside `aes()` maps a column; outside sets a fixed value.
- `geom_col()` draws heights you have; `geom_bar()` counts rows.
- A plot that runs isn't necessarily right -- an empty or flat plot is a clue, and warnings about removed rows tell you what's missing.
- Scripts should run on any computer: relative paths and Projects, not someone else's `setwd()`.

### Up next

Everything so far has been about producing your own output. Module 6 is about reading output a model produced, and judging whether it's any good.

```{r setup-module6, context="setup", include=FALSE}
# Demo data for the linear-vs-curved recognition quizzes -- pure visual aids,
# rendered at knit time only, so no globalenv() placement needed.
set.seed(42)
demo_linear_x <- 1:30
demo_linear_y <- 2 * demo_linear_x + rnorm(30, sd = 3)

demo_curved_x <- 1:30
demo_curved_y <- 0.5 * demo_curved_x^2 + rnorm(30, sd = 20)

# Data for the RMSE and "which model wins" exercises. Referenced by
# exercise_server()'s eval(parse(text = user_code), envir = new.env()) -- see
# Module 4's setup chunk note for why that means globalenv().
actual_weights <- c(45, 62, 58, 71, 39)
predicted_weights <- c(50, 55, 60, 68, 42)

actual_values <- c(120, 340, 210, 95, 275)
predicted_model_a <- c(150, 300, 260, 130, 230)
predicted_model_b <- c(125, 335, 205, 100, 270)

for (nm in c("actual_weights", "predicted_weights", "actual_values", "predicted_model_a", "predicted_model_b")) {
  assign(nm, get(nm), envir = globalenv())
}

evaluate_lm_slope_exercise <- function(user_code, result, envir, stage) {
  correct_model <- lm(weight_g ~ length_mm, data = fish_clean)
  correct_slope <- unname(coef(correct_model)["length_mm"])
  uses_lm <- grepl("lm\\s*\\(", user_code)
  uses_coef <- grepl("coef\\s*\\(", user_code)
  is_single <- is.numeric(result) && length(result) == 1
  correct_result <- is_single && isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(result), correct_slope, tolerance = 0.001))
  passed <- uses_lm && uses_coef && correct_result

  feedback_message <- if (passed) {
    paste0(
      "Right -- the slope is about ", round(correct_slope, 3),
      ": each extra mm of length goes with about ", round(correct_slope, 2), " more grams of weight."
    )
  } else if (identical(stage, "error_check")) {
    "That code doesn't run as-is -- check the formula inside lm() is outcome ~ predictor, with real column names."
  } else if (!uses_lm || !uses_coef) {
    "Keep both steps: fit the model with lm(), then pull the slope out with coef()."
  } else if (is_single && is.na(result)) {
    "NA means the model has no length_mm coefficient at all -- so length_mm isn't being used as a predictor. In lm(), which side of ~ is the thing you're predicting?"
  } else {
    "The model runs, but that isn't the slope for length_mm yet -- the question is how weight depends on length."
  }

  list(passed = passed, message = feedback_message)
}

evaluate_rmse_exercise <- function(user_code, result, envir, stage) {
  uses_given_vectors <- grepl("actual_weights", user_code) && grepl("predicted_weights", user_code)
  correct_rmse <- sqrt(mean((actual_weights - predicted_weights)^2))
  is_numeric_result <- is.numeric(result) && length(result) == 1
  result_ok <- is_numeric_result && isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(result), correct_rmse, tolerance = 0.01))
  still_zero <- is_numeric_result && isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(result), 0))

  passed <- uses_given_vectors && result_ok

  feedback_message <- if (passed) {
    paste0("That's right -- an RMSE of about ", round(correct_rmse, 2), " grams. The bug was one misplaced parenthesis.")
  } else if (identical(stage, "error_check")) {
    "That code doesn't run as-is -- check that every ( has a matching )."
  } else if (!uses_given_vectors) {
    "Compute it from actual_weights and predicted_weights, not typed-in numbers."
  } else if (still_zero) {
    "Still 0 -- a perfect model, which the data clearly isn't. Trace it: is each difference squared before averaging, or is the average taken first? (The misses above and below cancel out.)"
  } else if (!is_numeric_result) {
    "This should end up as a single number."
  } else {
    "Not the RMSE yet -- square each difference, then average, then take the square root."
  }

  list(passed = passed, message = feedback_message)
}

evaluate_module6_cumulative_exercise <- function(user_code, result, envir, stage) {
  has_rmse_a <- exists("rmse_a", envir = envir, inherits = FALSE) && is.numeric(get("rmse_a", envir = envir))
  has_rmse_b <- exists("rmse_b", envir = envir, inherits = FALSE) && is.numeric(get("rmse_b", envir = envir))

  correct_rmse_a <- sqrt(mean((actual_values - predicted_model_a)^2))
  correct_rmse_b <- sqrt(mean((actual_values - predicted_model_b)^2))
  rmse_a_ok <- has_rmse_a && isTRUE(all.equal(get("rmse_a", envir = envir), correct_rmse_a, tolerance = 0.01))
  rmse_b_ok <- has_rmse_b && isTRUE(all.equal(get("rmse_b", envir = envir), correct_rmse_b, tolerance = 0.01))

  has_better_model <- exists("better_model", envir = envir, inherits = FALSE)
  better_model_val <- if (has_better_model) toupper(trimws(as.character(get("better_model", envir = envir)))) else NA_character_
  better_model_ok <- has_better_model && identical(better_model_val, "B")

  passed <- rmse_a_ok && rmse_b_ok && better_model_ok

  feedback_message <- if (passed) {
    paste0(
      "Right -- Model A's RMSE is about ", round(correct_rmse_a, 1),
      " and Model B's is about ", round(correct_rmse_b, 1), ", so Model B wins."
    )
  } else if (identical(stage, "error_check")) {
    "That code doesn't run as-is -- work through it one line at a time."
  } else if (!has_rmse_a || !rmse_a_ok) {
    "Keep the rmse_a line as given -- it's already correct."
  } else if (!has_rmse_b || !rmse_b_ok) {
    "rmse_b isn't right yet -- compute it the same way as rmse_a, but with predicted_model_b."
  } else if (!has_better_model) {
    "better_model doesn't exist yet -- assign it \"A\" or \"B\"."
  } else {
    "Both RMSEs look right, but better_model isn't the one with the lower RMSE -- for RMSE, lower is better."
  }

  list(passed = passed, message = feedback_message)
}
```

```{r, context="server"}
  wrong_a = list(correct = FALSE, message = "A's 5 g is on fish it has already seen. On new fish it's off by 60 g -- far worse than B. That gap is the classic sign a model memorized its training data."),
  wrong_either = list(correct = FALSE, message = "They behave very differently on new fish: 60 g vs. 28 g. That's the number that matters for predicting new fish."),
  wrong_r2 = list(correct = FALSE, message = "RMSE on new data already answers this -- both are in grams, predicting the same thing.")
))

quiz_question_server(input, output, session, "rmse_units_quiz", module_number = 6, list(
  correct = list(correct = TRUE, message = "Correct -- RMSE is in the same units as the outcome, so an RMSE in kilograms and one in grams aren't on the same scale."),
  wrong_unitless = list(correct = FALSE, message = "RMSE is NOT unitless -- it carries the units of whatever you're predicting, which is exactly why comparing across units is misleading."),
  wrong_grams = list(correct = FALSE, message = "RMSE works the same way in any units -- the issue is comparing two DIFFERENT units to each other.")
))
```

## Module 6: Welcome back

From here on, you'll often be handed a script someone else wrote -- an instructor, a teammate, an AI -- that fits a model and prints results. This module is about **reading** that output: what a model is predicting, whether it's a good fit, and whether one model really beats another. You won't build anything beyond `lm()` itself.

<details>
<summary><strong>New to models?</strong> What "a model" means here.</summary>

A model is a rule for **predicting one thing from others** -- for example, predicting a fish's weight from its length. A straight-line model says "weight goes up by about the same amount for every extra millimeter." The model learns that amount from data, then uses it to make predictions. Everything in this module is about checking how good those predictions are.

</details>

## Module 6: Is it a line, or a curve?

Before trusting a straight-line model, look at the data's shape: a model that assumes a straight line will miss in a predictable pattern if the real relationship curves.

```{r linear-demo, echo=TRUE, fig.height=3}
plot(demo_linear_x, demo_linear_y, main = "Relationship A", xlab = "x", ylab = "y", pch = 19, col = "steelblue")
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
quiz_question_ui("linear_shape_quiz", "Look at \"Relationship A\" above. Does it look like a straight line or a curve?", c(
  "A straight line" = "correct",
  "A curve" = "wrong_curve"
))
```

```{r curved-demo, echo=TRUE, fig.height=3}
plot(demo_curved_x, demo_curved_y, main = "Relationship B", xlab = "x", ylab = "y", pch = 19, col = "darkorange")
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
quiz_question_ui("curved_shape_quiz", "Look at \"Relationship B\" above. Does it look like a straight line or a curve?", c(
  "A curve" = "correct",
  "A straight line" = "wrong_line"
))
```

## Module 6: Linear regression

`lm()` fits the best straight line through your data. Its first argument is a **formula**: `outcome ~ predictor`, read "outcome, predicted from predictor." The column on the **left** of `~` is what the model predicts. Everything on the **right** is used to predict it: `weight_g ~ length_mm + lake_site` uses two predictors, and `weight_g ~ .` uses every other column. You'll see this same formula in almost every R modeling function, not just `lm()`.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
quiz_question_ui("lm_formula_quiz", "In lm(weight_g ~ length_mm + lake_site, data = fish_clean), which column is the model trying to predict?", c(
  "weight_g" = "correct",
  "length_mm" = "wrong_length",
  "length_mm and lake_site" = "wrong_right",
  "Every column in fish_clean" = "wrong_all"
))
```

`summary()` shows what the model found:

```{r lm-demo, echo=TRUE}
model <- lm(weight_g ~ length_mm, data = fish_clean)
summary(model)
```

The pieces that matter most:

- Under **Coefficients**, the **Estimate** in the `length_mm` row is the **slope**: how much `weight_g` typically changes for each extra 1 mm of length.
- The `(Intercept)` Estimate is where the line would cross at `length_mm = 0` -- part of the equation, but not meaningful on its own here (no fish is 0 mm long).
- **Multiple R-squared** is the share of the variation in weight that the line accounts for (next topic).

```{r, echo=FALSE}
quiz_question_ui("lm_output_quiz", "In the printout above, which number tells you how much weight_g changes for each extra mm of length_mm?", c(
  "The Estimate in the length_mm row" = "correct",
  "The Estimate in the (Intercept) row" = "wrong_intercept",
  "The Multiple R-squared value" = "wrong_r2"
))
```

### Practice: fix the model

This is supposed to answer "how many extra grams of weight go with each extra millimeter of length?" -- but it prints `NA`. Fix it.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
exercise_ui("lm_slope_exercise", "model <- lm(length_mm ~ weight_g, data = fish_clean)\ncoef(model)[\"length_mm\"]")
```

## Module 6: R-squared -- how much does this explain?

**R-squared (R^2^)**, between 0 and 1, is how much of the up-and-down variation in the outcome a model accounts for:

$$
R^2 = 1 - \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}(\text{actual}_i - \text{predicted}_i)^2}{\sum_{i=1}^{n}(\text{actual}_i - \overline{\text{actual}})^2}
$$

The bottom of the fraction is how much the actual values vary around their average; the top is how much of that the model still misses. One minus "fraction missed" is "fraction explained."

Closer to 1 is generally better -- but R^2^ doesn't tell you whether the model is the right *shape*. That's why you look at the plot as well as the number.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
quiz_question_ui("r_squared_quiz", "A straight-line model fit to clearly curved data has an R-squared of 0.91. What should you conclude?", c(
  "It explains a lot of the variation, but the shape is wrong, so it will miss in a predictable pattern -- check the plot" = "correct",
  "0.91 is high, so the straight line is the right model" = "wrong_great",
  "An R-squared over 0.9 means the data were entered wrong" = "wrong_data",
  "The model is useless and explains nothing" = "wrong_useless"
))
```

## Module 6: RMSE -- how far off are the guesses?

**RMSE (root mean squared error)** answers a concrete question: how far off are the predictions, typically?

$$
\text{RMSE} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(\text{actual}_i - \text{predicted}_i)^2}
$$

In words: subtract to get each miss, **square** each miss (so misses above and below both count, and big ones count extra), average those, then take the square root to get back to the original units. An RMSE of 12 grams means predictions are typically off by around 12 grams. Lower is better.

### Practice: check the AI's RMSE

An AI wrote this line to compute RMSE for a model's weight predictions. It runs and reports **0** -- a perfect model. Look at the two vectors (`actual_weights` is 45, 62, 58, 71, 39; `predicted_weights` is 50, 55, 60, 68, 42). Is that believable? Find and fix the bug.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
exercise_ui("rmse_exercise", "sqrt(mean(actual_weights - predicted_weights)^2)")
```

## Module 6: Training data vs. new data

A model learns from **training data**. What you actually care about is how it does on **new data** it hasn't seen -- so scripts usually hold some data back as a **test set** and report the error there. A model can look excellent on its training data simply by memorizing it, then do badly on anything new. A big gap between training error and test error is the warning sign.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
quiz_question_ui("train_test_quiz", "Model A: RMSE of 5 g on the fish it was trained on, 60 g on new fish. Model B: 25 g on its training fish, 28 g on new fish. Which would you use to predict the weight of new fish?", c(
  "Model B" = "correct",
  "Model A -- its training error is far lower" = "wrong_a",
  "Either one -- they were trained on the same kind of data" = "wrong_either",
  "Can't tell without R-squared" = "wrong_r2"
))
```

## Module 6: Comparing two models

To compare two models, use the **same test data** and the **same outcome**: lower RMSE wins, higher R^2^ wins. And RMSE only compares within the same units -- an RMSE in kilograms and one in grams aren't on the same scale.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
quiz_question_ui("rmse_units_quiz", "Why can't you directly compare an RMSE of 0.03 (predicting weight in kilograms) to an RMSE of 30 (predicting weight in grams) and conclude the first model is far better?", c(
  "RMSE is in the units of what's being predicted, and kilograms and grams aren't the same scale" = "correct",
  "You can -- RMSE is unitless, so smaller is always better" = "wrong_unitless",
  "RMSE only works correctly when the units are grams" = "wrong_grams"
))
```

### Practice: which model wins?

`actual_values` holds the real weights for five fish; `predicted_model_a` and `predicted_model_b` are two models' predictions for those same fish. `rmse_a` is done for you. Compute `rmse_b` the same way, then set `better_model` to `"A"` or `"B"` -- whichever has the lower error.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
exercise_ui("module6_cumulative_exercise", "rmse_a <- sqrt(mean((actual_values - predicted_model_a)^2))\n")
```

## Module 6: Wrapping up

**If you remember only a few things from this module:**

- In `outcome ~ predictors`, the left side is what's predicted. Read the formula first, and you know what a model is for.
- Look at the shape of the data, not just R^2^ -- a high R^2^ can hide the wrong shape.
- RMSE is in the units of the outcome, and lower is better -- but only error on **new** data tells you how a model will really do.
- Model code that runs is not proof it's right. A "perfect" result is a reason to check, not celebrate.

That's exactly what the capstone preview asks of you: a real script fits two models to real fish data and reports their error on held-out fish, and your job is to read that output and decide what it's telling you.

```{r setup-module7, context="setup", include=FALSE}
# Question generators for the Extra Practice module. Each module (2-6) now
# has a POOL of generators -- module_practice_server() picks one at random
# from the current module's pool every time a new question is requested
# (module switch or "New Question" click) -- deliberately mixing types
# tied to that module's own graded exercises with types that AREN'T, per
# the app owner's explicit direction: practice should draw on everything a
# module taught, not just repeat its existing exercise shapes.
#
# Each generator is a zero-argument function returning list(prompt=,
# starting_code=, has_plot_output= [optional, default FALSE], check=).
# `check` is called as check(user_code, result, envir, stage) -- exactly
# like exercise_server()'s evaluate_fn -- so a generator whose question can
# genuinely error (e.g. a "fix the bug" type) can give a specific hint on
# "error_check" rather than a generic message. See module_practice_ui()/
# module_practice_server() in R/tutor_utils.R for the full contract -- in
# particular, why the random values below are baked directly into
# `prompt`/`starting_code` as literal text rather than stored in a shared
# variable: this data is per-question, not identical across every student's
# session the way e.g. Module 4's fish_clean is, so it can't safely live in
# globalenv() the way that reference data does. (Relatedly: a generator
# must NEVER have its questions call library() -- attaching a package is a
# process-wide side effect in R, not scoped to eval()'s envir argument, so
# it would leak across every concurrent student's session.)

# ---- Module 2 pool ----------------------------------------------------

generate_module2_comment_practice <- function() {
  keep_msg <- sample(c("Keep this one running", "Do not touch this line", "This line should stay active"), 1)
  comment_msg <- sample(c("Turn this into a comment", "This line should not run", "Comment this one out"), 1)

  list(
    prompt = sprintf('Below, comment out the SECOND line only (the one that says "%s"), so it does not run -- without deleting it or changing the first line.', comment_msg),
    starting_code = sprintf('print("%s")\nprint("%s")', keep_msg, comment_msg),
    check = function(user_code, result, envir, stage) {
      if (identical(stage, "error_check")) {
        return(list(passed = FALSE, message = "That code doesn't run as-is -- check that both lines are still valid R (or safely commented out)."))
      }
      keep_active <- grepl(paste0('(?m)^\\s*print\\("', keep_msg, '"\\)\\s*$'), user_code, perl = TRUE)
      comment_present <- grepl(paste0('(?m)^\\s*#.*', comment_msg), user_code, perl = TRUE)
      comment_still_active <- grepl(paste0('(?m)^\\s*print\\("', comment_msg, '"\\)\\s*$'), user_code, perl = TRUE)
      passed <- keep_active && comment_present && !comment_still_active

      message <- if (passed) {
        "Correct -- the first line still runs, and the second is safely commented out."
      } else if (!keep_active) {
        "The first line got changed or removed -- it should stay exactly as it was."
      } else if (comment_still_active) {
        "The second line is still active R code -- put a # in front of it to comment it out."
      } else {
        "Add a # before the second line to comment it out."
      }
      list(passed = passed, message = message)
    }
  )
}

generate_module2_fix_bug_practice <- function() {
  # NOT tied to either of Module 2's own graded exercises (comment-out,
  # fix-the-bug's specific wording) -- a fresh set of syntax bugs, framed
  # around "reading an error message" rather than reproducing the exact
  # graded exercise. Genuinely errors until fixed, so the error_check
  # branch below is what actually shows while the student is still working.
  bugs <- list(
    list(broken = 'print("Nice to meet you)', hint = "a closing quote", correct = "Nice to meet you"),
    list(broken = "sum(4, 8, 15", hint = "a closing parenthesis", correct = 27),
    list(broken = "mean(c(10, 20, 30)", hint = "a closing parenthesis", correct = 20)
  )
  chosen <- bugs[[sample(seq_along(bugs), 1)]]

  list(
    prompt = sprintf("The line below has a bug and won't run -- it's missing %s. Fix it so it runs without an error.", chosen$hint),
    starting_code = chosen$broken,
    check = function(user_code, result, envir, stage) {
      if (identical(stage, "error_check")) {
        return(list(passed = FALSE, message = sprintf("Still doesn't run -- look closely for %s.", chosen$hint)))
      }
      passed <- isTRUE(all.equal(result, chosen$correct))
      message <- if (passed) "Correct -- that runs cleanly now." else "It runs now, but the result doesn't look right -- check you didn't change anything besides fixing the bug."
      list(passed = passed, message = message)
    }
  )
}

# ---- Module 3 pool ----------------------------------------------------

generate_module3_vector_practice <- function() {
  # Difficulty lever used here: no FIXME -- the code box starts with just
  # the vector itself, and the student writes the whole indexing
  # expression from scratch.
  n <- sample(4:7, 1)
  values <- sample(1:50, n)
  idx <- sample(seq_len(n), 1)
  correct <- values[idx]
  value_str <- paste(values, collapse = ", ")

  list(
    prompt = sprintf(
      "Given practice_vec <- c(%s), write your own code below that returns the value at position %d. (No FIXME this time -- write the whole line yourself.)",
      value_str, idx
    ),
    starting_code = sprintf("practice_vec <- c(%s)\n", value_str),
    check = function(user_code, result, envir, stage) {
      if (identical(stage, "error_check")) {
        return(list(passed = FALSE, message = "That code doesn't run as-is -- check your syntax."))
      }
      uses_vec <- grepl("practice_vec", user_code)
      uses_index <- grepl("\\[", user_code)
      correct_result <- is.numeric(result) && length(result) == 1 && isTRUE(result == correct)
      passed <- uses_vec && uses_index && correct_result

      message <- if (passed) {
        sprintf("Correct -- position %d is %d.", idx, correct)
      } else if (!uses_vec) {
        "This should be computed from practice_vec directly, not a typed-in number."
      } else if (!uses_index) {
        "Use square brackets to index into the vector, like practice_vec[...]."
      } else {
        sprintf("Not quite -- double check you're asking for position %d specifically.", idx)
      }
      list(passed = passed, message = message)
    }
  )
}

generate_module3_formula_practice <- function() {
  # Tied to Module 3's own "Turning a formula into code" exercise, but with
  # 3 different formulas randomized between -- reinforces the same skill
  # with real variety rather than the exact same formula every time.
  templates <- list(
    function() {
      l <- sample(2:20, 1)
      w <- sample(2:20, 1)
      correct <- l * w
      list(
        prompt = sprintf("The area of a rectangle is A = l x w. If l = %d and w = %d, write code that computes A.", l, w),
        starting_code = sprintf("l <- %d\nw <- %d\nFIXME", l, w),
        check = function(user_code, result, envir, stage) {
          if (identical(stage, "error_check")) return(list(passed = FALSE, message = "That code doesn't run as-is -- check that FIXME is replaced with a complete expression."))
          passed <- is.numeric(result) && length(result) == 1 && isTRUE(result == correct)
          list(passed = passed, message = if (passed) sprintf("Correct -- the area is %d.", correct) else "Not quite -- check the formula A = l * w.")
        }
      )
    },
    function() {
      a <- sample(3:15, 1)
      b <- sample(3:15, 1)
      correct <- sqrt(a^2 + b^2)
      list(
        prompt = sprintf("Using the Pythagorean theorem c = sqrt(a^2 + b^2), with a = %d and b = %d, write code that computes c.", a, b),
        starting_code = sprintf("a <- %d\nb <- %d\nFIXME", a, b),
        check = function(user_code, result, envir, stage) {
          if (identical(stage, "error_check")) return(list(passed = FALSE, message = "That code doesn't run as-is -- check that FIXME is replaced with a complete expression."))
          uses_sqrt <- grepl("sqrt\\s*\\(", user_code)
          correct_result <- is.numeric(result) && length(result) == 1 && isTRUE(all.equal(result, correct, tolerance = 0.001))
          passed <- uses_sqrt && correct_result
          message <- if (passed) {
            sprintf("Correct -- c is about %.2f.", correct)
          } else if (!uses_sqrt) {
            "Don't forget the square root -- this formula needs sqrt()."
          } else {
            "Not quite -- check that both a and b are squared before adding them."
          }
          list(passed = passed, message = message)
        }
      )
    },
    function() {
      celsius <- sample(-10:40, 1)
      correct <- celsius * 9 / 5 + 32
      list(
        prompt = sprintf("Using F = C x 9/5 + 32, with C = %d, write code that computes F.", celsius),
        starting_code = sprintf("celsius <- %d\nFIXME", celsius),
        check = function(user_code, result, envir, stage) {
          if (identical(stage, "error_check")) return(list(passed = FALSE, message = "That code doesn't run as-is -- check that FIXME is replaced with a complete expression."))
          passed <- is.numeric(result) && length(result) == 1 && isTRUE(all.equal(result, correct, tolerance = 0.01))
          list(passed = passed, message = if (passed) sprintf("Correct -- that's %.1f°F.", correct) else "Not quite -- check the formula F = C * 9/5 + 32.")
        }
      )
    }
  )
  templates[[sample(seq_along(templates), 1)]]()
}

generate_module3_datatype_practice <- function() {
  # NOT tied to any of Module 3's graded exercises -- "data types" is
  # taught (the module's very first topic) but never itself graded.
  cases <- list(
    list(value_code = "42", type_fn = "is.numeric", label = "a number"),
    list(value_code = '"hello"', type_fn = "is.character", label = "text (a string)"),
    list(value_code = "TRUE", type_fn = "is.logical", label = "a logical (TRUE/FALSE) value")
  )
  chosen <- cases[[sample(seq_along(cases), 1)]]

  list(
    prompt = sprintf(
      "Given practice_value <- %s, write code that checks whether practice_value is %s -- it should return TRUE.",
      chosen$value_code, chosen$label
    ),
    starting_code = sprintf("practice_value <- %s\n", chosen$value_code),
    check = function(user_code, result, envir, stage) {
      if (identical(stage, "error_check")) return(list(passed = FALSE, message = "That code doesn't run as-is -- check your syntax."))
      uses_value <- grepl("practice_value", user_code)
      uses_fn <- grepl(paste0(chosen$type_fn, "\\s*\\("), user_code)
      correct_result <- is.logical(result) && length(result) == 1 && isTRUE(result == TRUE)
      passed <- uses_value && uses_fn && correct_result
      message <- if (passed) {
        sprintf("Correct -- %s(practice_value) is TRUE.", chosen$type_fn)
      } else if (!uses_fn) {
        sprintf("Try using %s() -- that's the function that checks for this type.", chosen$type_fn)
      } else if (!uses_value) {
        "This should check practice_value directly, not a typed-in value."
      } else {
        "Not quite -- double check which function tests for this type."
      }
      list(passed = passed, message = message)
    }
  )
}

# ---- Module 4 pool ----------------------------------------------------

generate_module4_pipeline_practice <- function() {
  # Difficulty lever used here: combine multiple skills, no FIXME -- a
  # full cumulative pipeline (filter, group_by, summarize, arrange -- all
  # four, like Module 4's own cumulative exercise), on a bigger table with
  # an extra column.
  fruits <- c("apple", "banana", "cherry", "date", "elderberry")
  stores <- c("Downtown", "Uptown", "Eastside")
  exclude_fruit <- sample(fruits, 1)
  n <- sample(10:14, 1)
  fruit_col <- sample(fruits, n, replace = TRUE)
  store_col <- sample(stores, n, replace = TRUE)
  count_col <- sample(5:40, n)

  df <- data.frame(fruit = fruit_col, store = store_col, count = count_col, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  correct <- df |>
    filter(fruit != exclude_fruit) |>
    group_by(store) |>
    summarize(total = sum(count), .groups = "drop") |>
    arrange(desc(total))

  fruit_str <- paste(sprintf('"%s"', fruit_col), collapse = ", ")
  store_str <- paste(sprintf('"%s"', store_col), collapse = ", ")
  count_str <- paste(count_col, collapse = ", ")

  list(
    prompt = sprintf(
      'practice_df has fruit, store, and count columns. Filter OUT all "%s" rows, then group what remains by store, compute the total (sum) count per store, and sort from highest total to lowest. (No FIXME -- write the full pipeline yourself, using filter(), group_by(), summarize(), and arrange().)',
      exclude_fruit
    ),
    starting_code = sprintf(
      "practice_df <- data.frame(fruit = c(%s), store = c(%s), count = c(%s))\n",
      fruit_str, store_str, count_str
    ),
    check = function(user_code, result, envir, stage) {
      if (identical(stage, "error_check")) return(list(passed = FALSE, message = "That code doesn't run as-is -- work through it one step at a time."))
      uses_filter <- grepl("filter\\s*\\(", user_code)
      uses_group_by <- grepl("group_by\\s*\\(", user_code)
      uses_summarize <- grepl("summari[sz]e\\s*\\(", user_code)
      uses_arrange <- grepl("arrange\\s*\\(", user_code)
      is_df <- is.data.frame(result) && "total" %in% names(result)
      order_ok <- is_df && nrow(result) == nrow(correct) && isTRUE(all.equal(result$total, correct$total))
      passed <- uses_filter && uses_group_by && uses_summarize && uses_arrange && order_ok

      message <- if (passed) {
        "Correct -- filtered, grouped, summed, and sorted correctly."
      } else if (!uses_filter) {
        sprintf('Start with filter() to remove the "%s" rows.', exclude_fruit)
      } else if (!uses_group_by) {
        "Add a group_by(store) step next."
      } else if (!uses_summarize) {
        "Use summarize() to compute the total (sum) count per store."
      } else if (!is_df || !order_ok) {
        "Close, but the totals or the order aren't quite right yet -- check the filter/sum, then arrange(desc(...))."
      } else {
        "Not quite -- double check each step of the pipeline."
      }
      list(passed = passed, message = message)
    }
  )
}

generate_module4_indexing_practice <- function() {
  # Tied to Module 4's own indexing exercise, but square-bracket indexing
  # (not dplyr) on fresh data -- reinforces the base-R alternative dplyr is
  # usually preferred over, which the module explicitly calls out.
  sites <- c("North Lake", "South Lake", "East Pond")
  target_site <- sample(sites, 1)
  n <- sample(6:9, 1)
  site_col <- sample(sites, n, replace = TRUE)
  weight_col <- sample(50:400, n)
  correct_n <- sum(site_col == target_site)

  site_str <- paste(sprintf('"%s"', site_col), collapse = ", ")
  weight_str <- paste(weight_col, collapse = ", ")

  list(
    prompt = sprintf(
      'practice_df has site and weight columns. Using square-bracket indexing (practice_df[...]), NOT a dplyr verb, return only the rows where site equals "%s".',
      target_site
    ),
    starting_code = sprintf("practice_df <- data.frame(site = c(%s), weight = c(%s))\n", site_str, weight_str),
    check = function(user_code, result, envir, stage) {
      if (identical(stage, "error_check")) return(list(passed = FALSE, message = "That code doesn't run as-is -- check the brackets and commas."))
      uses_bracket <- grepl("\\[", user_code)
      not_dplyr <- !grepl("filter\\s*\\(", user_code)
      correct_result <- is.data.frame(result) && nrow(result) == correct_n && all(result$site == target_site)
      passed <- uses_bracket && not_dplyr && correct_result
      message <- if (passed) {
        sprintf('Correct -- %d rows match "%s".', correct_n, target_site)
      } else if (!not_dplyr) {
        "Use square-bracket indexing here (practice_df[ ... , ]), not a dplyr verb -- that's the point of this one."
      } else if (!uses_bracket) {
        "Use square brackets, like practice_df[practice_df$site == ..., ]."
      } else {
        sprintf('Not quite -- double check the row count and that only "%s" rows are included.', target_site)
      }
      list(passed = passed, message = message)
    }
  )
}

generate_module4_inspect_practice <- function() {
  # NOT tied to any of Module 4's graded exercises -- "Inspecting a data
  # frame" is its own taught topic with no dedicated exercise of its own.
  n <- sample(8:20, 1)
  values <- round(runif(n, 1, 100), 1)
  value_str <- paste(values, collapse = ", ")
  col_name <- sample(c("weight", "length", "score", "amount"), 1)

  list(
    prompt = sprintf("practice_df has one column, %s, with %d rows. Write code that returns the number of rows in practice_df.", col_name, n),
    starting_code = sprintf("practice_df <- data.frame(%s = c(%s))\n", col_name, value_str),
    check = function(user_code, result, envir, stage) {
      if (identical(stage, "error_check")) return(list(passed = FALSE, message = "That code doesn't run as-is -- check your syntax."))
      passed <- is.numeric(result) && length(result) == 1 && isTRUE(result == n)
      message <- if (passed) sprintf("Correct -- practice_df has %d rows.", n) else "Not quite -- try nrow(practice_df)."
      list(passed = passed, message = message)
    }
  )
}

# ---- Module 5 pool ----------------------------------------------------

generate_module5_scaffolded_practice <- function() {
  # More scaffolding than the beta version had -- FIXME blanks are back,
  # not a blank-slate rewrite. Still combines filter + plot + title (like
  # Module 5's own cumulative exercise), on an added category column.
  categories <- c("A", "B", "C")
  n <- sample(24:36, 1)
  cat_col <- sample(categories, n, replace = TRUE)
  x_vals <- round(runif(n, 1, 50), 1)
  y_vals <- round(x_vals * runif(1, 0.5, 2) + rnorm(n, sd = 5), 1)
  target_cat <- sample(categories, 1)

  cat_str <- paste(sprintf('"%s"', cat_col), collapse = ", ")
  x_str <- paste(x_vals, collapse = ", ")
  y_str <- paste(y_vals, collapse = ", ")

  list(
    prompt = sprintf(
      'practice_df has columns category, x, and y. Filter down to just category "%s", then create a scatter plot of x vs. y with any title you like. Replace all three FIXMEs.',
      target_cat
    ),
    starting_code = sprintf(
      "practice_df <- data.frame(category = c(%s), x = c(%s), y = c(%s))\npractice_df |>\n  filter(category == FIXME) |>\n  ggplot(aes(x = FIXME, y = FIXME)) +\n  geom_point() +\n  labs(title = FIXME)",
      cat_str, x_str, y_str
    ),
    has_plot_output = TRUE,
    check = function(user_code, result, envir, stage) {
      if (identical(stage, "error_check")) return(list(passed = FALSE, message = "That code doesn't run as-is -- work through it one FIXME at a time."))
      uses_filter <- grepl("filter\\s*\\(", user_code)
      is_ggplot <- inherits(result, "ggplot")
      has_point_layer <- is_ggplot && any(vapply(result$layers, function(l) inherits(l$geom, "GeomPoint"), logical(1)))
      right_n <- is_ggplot && is.data.frame(result$data) && nrow(result$data) == sum(cat_col == target_cat)
      x_ok <- is_ggplot && identical(rlang::as_label(result$mapping$x), "x")
      y_ok <- is_ggplot && identical(rlang::as_label(result$mapping$y), "y")
      has_title <- is_ggplot && is.character(result$labels$title) && nzchar(trimws(result$labels$title))
      passed <- uses_filter && is_ggplot && has_point_layer && right_n && x_ok && y_ok && has_title

      message <- if (passed) {
        sprintf('Correct -- filtered to "%s", plotted, and titled.', target_cat)
      } else if (!uses_filter || !right_n) {
        sprintf('Check the filter() FIXME -- this should only include the "%s" rows.', target_cat)
      } else if (!has_point_layer) {
        "This needs a geom_point() layer."
      } else if (!x_ok) {
        "The x-axis FIXME isn't mapped to x yet."
      } else if (!y_ok) {
        "The y-axis FIXME isn't mapped to y yet."
      } else {
        "The plot looks right, but the title FIXME still needs replacing -- any text in quotes works."
      }
      list(passed = passed, message = message)
    }
  )
}

generate_module5_fix_plot_practice <- function() {
  # NOT tied to any of Module 5's graded exercises -- all of those are
  # "fill in the FIXME" style; this is "find and fix the bug" instead,
  # closer to how ggplot code gets used in practice (reading/adjusting
  # something already mostly written, not composing from a blank page).
  n <- sample(15:25, 1)
  x_vals <- round(runif(n, 1, 50), 1)
  y_vals <- round(x_vals * runif(1, 0.5, 2) + rnorm(n, sd = 5), 1)
  x_str <- paste(x_vals, collapse = ", ")
  y_str <- paste(y_vals, collapse = ", ")

  bugs <- list(
    list(
      broken = sprintf("practice_df <- data.frame(x = c(%s), y = c(%s))\nggplot(practice_df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +\n  geom_pont()", x_str, y_str),
      hint = "the geom function name is misspelled"
    ),
    list(
      broken = sprintf("practice_df <- data.frame(x = c(%s), y = c(%s))\nggplot(practice_df, aes(x = y, y = x)) +\n  geom_point()", x_str, y_str),
      hint = "x and y are mapped to the wrong columns"
    )
  )
  chosen <- bugs[[sample(seq_along(bugs), 1)]]

  list(
    prompt = sprintf("The scatter plot code below has a bug -- %s. Find and fix it so it correctly plots x vs. y.", chosen$hint),
    starting_code = chosen$broken,
    has_plot_output = TRUE,
    check = function(user_code, result, envir, stage) {
      if (identical(stage, "error_check")) return(list(passed = FALSE, message = sprintf("Still doesn't run -- remember, %s.", chosen$hint)))
      is_ggplot <- inherits(result, "ggplot")
      has_point_layer <- is_ggplot && any(vapply(result$layers, function(l) inherits(l$geom, "GeomPoint"), logical(1)))
      x_ok <- is_ggplot && identical(rlang::as_label(result$mapping$x), "x")
      y_ok <- is_ggplot && identical(rlang::as_label(result$mapping$y), "y")
      passed <- is_ggplot && has_point_layer && x_ok && y_ok
      message <- if (passed) {
        "Correct -- fixed and plotting x vs. y properly now."
      } else if (!has_point_layer) {
        "Still not drawing points -- check the geom function name."
      } else {
        "Close, but x and y still aren't mapped correctly."
      }
      list(passed = passed, message = message)
    }
  )
}

# ---- Module 6 pool ----------------------------------------------------

generate_module6_rmse_practice <- function() {
  # More scaffolding than the beta version had: a formula reminder comment
  # is back in the starting code, since the point of repeated practice is
  # applying the idea quickly, not re-deriving the formula from memory
  # every single rep. Bigger/messier inputs (from the beta hardening pass)
  # are kept.
  n <- sample(8:12, 1)
  actual <- round(runif(n, 15, 250), 1)
  predicted <- round(actual + rnorm(n, sd = 12), 1)
  correct <- sqrt(mean((actual - predicted)^2))
  actual_str <- paste(actual, collapse = ", ")
  predicted_str <- paste(predicted, collapse = ", ")

  list(
    prompt = "practice_actual and practice_predicted are a model's actual and predicted values for the same cases. Compute the RMSE.",
    starting_code = sprintf(
      "# Reminder: RMSE = sqrt(mean((actual - predicted)^2))\npractice_actual <- c(%s)\npractice_predicted <- c(%s)\nsqrt(mean((practice_actual - practice_predicted)^FIXME))",
      actual_str, predicted_str
    ),
    check = function(user_code, result, envir, stage) {
      if (identical(stage, "error_check")) return(list(passed = FALSE, message = "That code doesn't run as-is -- check that FIXME is replaced with a number."))
      correct_result <- is.numeric(result) && length(result) == 1 && isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(result), correct, tolerance = 0.01))
      message <- if (correct_result) {
        sprintf("Correct -- RMSE is about %.2f.", correct)
      } else {
        "Not quite -- check the RMSE formula in the reminder comment above."
      }
      list(passed = correct_result, message = message)
    }
  )
}

generate_module6_rsquared_practice <- function() {
  # NOT tied to any of Module 6's graded exercises -- R-squared is taught
  # (with its own formula/MathJax section) but never itself graded; both
  # exercises are RMSE-based. Scaffolded with the same formula-reminder
  # pattern as the RMSE generator above.
  n <- sample(8:12, 1)
  actual <- round(runif(n, 15, 250), 1)
  predicted <- round(actual + rnorm(n, sd = 12), 1)
  correct <- 1 - sum((actual - predicted)^2) / sum((actual - mean(actual))^2)
  actual_str <- paste(actual, collapse = ", ")
  predicted_str <- paste(predicted, collapse = ", ")

  list(
    prompt = "practice_actual and practice_predicted are a model's actual and predicted values for the same cases. Compute R-squared.",
    starting_code = sprintf(
      "# Reminder: R-squared = 1 - sum((actual - predicted)^2) / sum((actual - mean(actual))^2)\npractice_actual <- c(%s)\npractice_predicted <- c(%s)\nFIXME",
      actual_str, predicted_str
    ),
    check = function(user_code, result, envir, stage) {
      if (identical(stage, "error_check")) return(list(passed = FALSE, message = "That code doesn't run as-is -- check that FIXME is replaced with a complete expression."))
      correct_result <- is.numeric(result) && length(result) == 1 && isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(result), correct, tolerance = 0.01))
      message <- if (correct_result) {
        sprintf("Correct -- R-squared is about %.3f.", correct)
      } else {
        "Not quite -- check the R-squared formula in the reminder comment above."
      }
      list(passed = correct_result, message = message)
    }
  )
}

MODULE_PRACTICE_GENERATORS <- list(
  "2" = list(generate_module2_comment_practice, generate_module2_fix_bug_practice),
  "3" = list(generate_module3_vector_practice, generate_module3_formula_practice, generate_module3_datatype_practice),
  "4" = list(generate_module4_pipeline_practice, generate_module4_indexing_practice, generate_module4_inspect_practice),
  "5" = list(generate_module5_scaffolded_practice, generate_module5_fix_plot_practice),
  "6" = list(generate_module6_rmse_practice, generate_module6_rsquared_practice)
)
```

```{r, context="server"}
# --- Practice chat + exercise wiring --------------------------------------
# NEW GOTCHA, found building this module: module_practice_ui()'s panel is
# entirely dynamic (a bare uiOutput(), filled in by renderUI() after the
# session starts) -- unlike every other exercise/quiz in this app, which
# emit fully static HTML at knit time (only their small feedback area is a
# uiOutput()). An earlier version of this module stacked two such dynamic
# panels as separate `###` sub-sections under one `##` topic, which
# silently broke learnr's progressive/allow_skip "Continue" gate between
# them -- it never unlocked no matter what was submitted, confirmed via the
# DOM directly (the locked `###` stayed a `display: none`
# `.section.level3.hide` div). Root cause, as best determined: that gate
# depends on markup present in the static HTML at knit time to recognize a
# section's exercise as completed, which a bare uiOutput() placeholder
# doesn't provide regardless of what's later rendered into it. Since this
# module is ungraded anyway (no reason to force sequential completion), the
# fix is to not use `###` subheadings for this content at all -- see the
# bold-text label below instead of `###`. Any FUTURE dynamic-UI content
# stacked under one `##` topic should do the same (flat, no `###`) unless
# this gets solved.
#
# One shared, ungraded practice chat for the whole module (not per-question
# -- there's no fixed exercise context to hang a separate panel off of).
wire_standalone_chat("tutor_chat_m7_practice", "tutor_accordion_m7_practice", "Ask for practice help", PRACTICE_SYSTEM_PROMPT, PRACTICE_CHAT_GREETING, input, output, session)

module_practice_server(input, output, session, "module_practice", MODULE_PRACTICE_GENERATORS)
```

## Module 7: Extra Practice

Everything up to here has been graded, one-shot content -- pass it once and move on. This module is different: it's **ungraded and endlessly repeatable**. Pick a module below and click "New Question" for a fresh version any time, as many times as you want, whenever you want more reps on a skill. Nothing here is tracked or scored -- it's just practice.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
accordion(
  id = "tutor_accordion_m7_practice",
  open = FALSE,
  accordion_panel(
    title = "Ask for practice help",
    chat_ui(
      "tutor_chat_m7_practice",
      placeholder = "Ask a question, or paste your current practice question or code...",
      greeting = PRACTICE_CHAT_GREETING,
      allow_attachments = FALSE
    )
  )
)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
))
```
